title: OA ChatCompletions payload sanitizer and tool-call conductor
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Create a compatibility layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (ChatCompletions-style) requests and reliably maps them onto Redwood's internal request/response model. Responsibilities: sanitize incoming payloads, normalize role/name/content shapes, validate and enforce structured output contracts, translate function/tool call fields into Redwood toolhook events, preserve streaming deltas and event ordering, and expose granular telemetry and fallbacks when fields are missing or malformed. The layer must be opt-in behind a runtime flag, support canary routing, and allow rollback without affecting existing Redwood-native API users.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OA ChatCompletions requests with messages/temperature/top_p/etc. are normalized to Redwood Request V2 with deterministic field mappings
Structured outputs declared via OA "function_call" and content filters are validated and enforced; invalid outputs trigger clearly documented fallback behaviors
Streaming events from OA-style 'delta' chunks are emitted by Redwood's streamer with identical ordering, token-level timestamps, and tool-call stubs when appropriate
Tool/function call objects (name, arguments, call_type) are converted into Redwood toolhook events and replayable call records
No regression in latency under 99th percentile for 1k RPS synthetic OA-compat workload during canary
Comprehensive unit + integration test coverage and a migration playbook for customers using OA clients
technical_notes: High-level design: lightweight shim sitting in front of API router -> transforms -> validator -> passthrough to runtime/streamer
Sanitization: strict schema validation for messages (role/name/content), allow legacy 'user'/'system' synonyms, strip unsupported fields with audit logs
Streaming: adopt event envelope that preserves OA delta chunks as 'delta' event type; include incremental token metadata to support client-side reconstruction
Tool-calls: map OA function_call to Redwood toolhook with deterministic idempotency key; embed original OA payload in 'raw_compat' header for debugging
Backward compatibility: if runtime flag off, requests pass through current gateway unchanged; feature-flag toggles live per-tenant
Telemetry: emit compatibility_migration.* spans with mapping version and payload size; surface token mapping rate in console
Error handling: 400 for invalid schema, 422 for contract violations that cannot be auto-corrected, 202+deferred for tool-call scheduling when target tool unavailable
Performance: transform path must be <2ms p50 additional latency; use precompiled mapping tables and JIT field extractors to avoid alloc storms
implementation_steps: 1) Draft compatibility mapping spec (fields, synonyms, streaming envelope) - draft complete
2) Implement request sanitizer + schema validator as middleware (unit tests)
3) Implement streaming envelope translator and delta re-emitter tied to existing stream runtime
4) Implement toolhook mapping with idempotency and retry policies; wire to tool execution queue
5) Add telemetry + logs + console metrics and a canary rollout plan
6) Run performance tests and iterate on allocations/hot paths
7) Write migration doc and sample client snippets (Node/Python)

testing_plan: Unit tests for each sanitization rule and synonym mapping
Property-based fuzzing for malformed OA payloads to ensure shim doesn't panic
E2E tests using recorded OA cassettes that exercise streaming, tool-calls, and structured output enforcement
Load tests: 1k/5k RPS simulated OA clients to validate latency SLOs and scaling behavior
Integration tests with console metrics to verify telemetry and rollout signaling
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal QA feature-flag enabled on staging cluster
Stage 1: canary (1% tenants) for 72 hours; rollback if 99p latency regresses or error rate >0.5%
Stage 2: expand to 25% after fixes and two clean 24h windows
Stage 3: global rollout for self-serve tenants; enterprise customers will be contacted with migration docs
Emergency: feature flag kill-switch at gateway + immediate autoscaling to mitigate backlog
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: subtle differences in OA streaming semantics could cause client-visible reordering - Mitigation: preserve original 'chunk_id' and deliver monotonic seq numbers
Risk: tool-call contract mismatch causes downstream tool errors - Mitigation: strict pre-execution validation with dry-run mode and clear failure codes
Risk: extra latency from transformation path - Mitigation: micro-benchmark and inline hot code paths; increase canary capacity
Risk: leakage of PII during raw payload audit logs - Mitigation: redact by default; make raw payload opt-in and logged to secure audit store
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on the sanitization whitelist (technical_notes #2) and the streaming envelope format. We need alignment on how we expose 'raw_compat' for audits without creating privacy exposure.
PM: Luca requested that fallback behaviors be explicitly documented in the migration guide
Design: ensure that client error codes map to human-readable messages for OA users migrating to Redwood
